nodes_add.name: Swami Ram (Rama Joo) of Srinagar
nodes_add.note: Kashmiri Shaiva teacher and Lakshmanjoo's family guru; dates given as 1852–1914 (Lakshmanjoo Academy) or 1854–1915 (other sources).

nodes_add.name: Swami Mahatab Kak
nodes_add.note: Chief disciple of Swami Ram; initiated Lakshmanjoo and taught him the Shaiva scriptures.

nodes_add.name: Lilian Silburn
nodes_add.note: French Indologist; studied with Lakshmanjoo from 1948 and translated Kashmiri Shaiva texts into French.

nodes_add.name: Jaideva Singh
nodes_add.note: Indian scholar and musicologist; studied with Lakshmanjoo and translated the Shiva Sutras, Spanda Karikas and Vijnana Bhairava into English.

nodes_add.name: Alexis Sanderson
nodes_add.note: Oxford scholar of Shaivism; spent six years in Kashmir studying with Lakshmanjoo.

nodes_add.name: John Hughes
nodes_add.note: American student of Lakshmanjoo from 1971; recorded and edited his English teachings (Universal Shaiva Fellowship / Lakshmanjoo Academy).

nodes_add.name: Ramamohana Brahmachari
nodes_add.note: Himalayan yogi whom Krishnamacharya named as his teacher; no independent record has been found.

nodes_add.name: Indra Devi
nodes_add.note: Born Eugenie Peterson in Riga; studied with Krishnamacharya in Mysore in the late 1930s; taught yoga in Shanghai, Hollywood and Argentina.

nodes_add.name: Srivatsa Ramaswami
nodes_add.note: Long-time student of Krishnamacharya in Madras; teaches vinyasa krama.

nodes_add.name: A.G. Mohan
nodes_add.note: Student of Krishnamacharya in Madras; author of Krishnamacharya: His Life and Teachings (2010).

nodes_update.name: Swami Lakshmanjoo
nodes_update.note: Born Lakshman Raina, Srinagar, 9 May 1907; died Noida, 27 September 1991.

nodes_update.name: T. Krishnamacharya
nodes_update.note: Born Muchukundapura, 18 November 1888; died Madras, 28 February 1989.

edges_upsert.note: Taught the Trika/Pratyabhijna system of Abhinavagupta; the claim of an unbroken chain of masters back to the medieval teachers rests on the tradition's account.
Line through Swami Manakak (fl. 1860) as presented by the Lakshmanjoo Academy.
Mahatab Kak was Swami Ram's chief disciple (G.N. Raina; Lakshmanjoo Academy).
Family guru; named the boy and taught him the Gayatri mantra (G.N. Raina).
Entrusted with the boy at about seven; initiated him (Ishwar Ashram Trust); formal initiation at seventeen per Stillness Speaks.
Studied and recorded in Kashmir 1971–1986; hosted Lakshmanjoo in Los Angeles in 1991.
Muktananda visited him (twice, per Wikipedia); Kashmir Shaivism became the philosophical frame of Siddha Yoga. Lighter branch.
Hatha yoga texts he cited and taught.
By Krishnamacharya's own account, seven and a half years of study in the Himalaya; journey usually dated c. 1919; no independent record.
Brother-in-law; lived with the family in Mysore.
Son and student; founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram, Madras, 1976.
Studied with him in Mysore in the late 1930s.

places.name: Ishwar Ashram, Ishber (above Gupta Ganga, near Nishat Bagh)
places.what: His house from 1934 and Ishwar Ashram, overlooking Dal Lake.

places.name: Harvan
places.what: Danyahama, where he studied with Maheshwar Nath Razdan.

places.name: Varanasi (Banaras)
places.what: Sanskrit and philosophical study from c. 1906.

glossary.def: Arrangement or placing in order; in Krishnamacharya's usage, a counted sequence of movements linked to the breath.
Recognition; the Kashmiri Shaiva school holding that liberation is recognising one's own nature as Shiva.
Threefold; Abhinavagupta's school of Kashmir Shaivism, named for its three goddesses and its triad of Shiva, Shakti and the individual.
Grace; in Kashmir Shaivism, the fifth of Shiva's five acts, by which he reveals his own nature.

lakshmanjoo: born 9 May 1907 Srinagar; died 27 Sept 1991 Noida; Swami Rama Joo 1854–1915; Mehatab Kak 1870–1942; Razdan 1926–1933; ashram 1962; Silburn 1948; Reps 1957; Muktananda visits; USF 1991; Gitartha Samgraha 1933 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshman_Joo

father Narayandas Raina, houseboats; mother Aranyamali; named by Swami Ram; Gayatri; entrusted to Mahtab Kak at seven; experience at 20 at 4 a.m.; Sadhuganga ashram at Sopore, then Danyahama, Harvan; Razdan seven years; ashram built 1934 -> https://ikashmir.net/gnraina/lakshmanjoo.html

Swami Ram 1852–1914; badhi bhod 'greater than the greatest'; glimpse at nineteen and celibacy vow; visitors from 1965; 'the last in an unbroken chain of Masters'; Manakak 1860 -> https://lakshmanjooacademy.org/swami-lakshmanjoo
formal initiation at seventeen; vow of lifelong celibacy; established Ishwara Ashram Trust; laid foundation for USF -> https://www.stillnessspeaks.com/teacher/swami-lakshmanjoo/
Hughes to Kashmir 1971 for PhD; fifteen years; left 1986; 8 books and 35 hours of video -> https://www.lakshmanjooacademy.org/editor-in-chief

84th birthday celebrated 11 April 1991 in LA; one of eighteen children; live 15 more years, mahasamadhi 2006; Gopi Krishna sought authentication, 'He didn't give it'; Kaviraj 'He was secretly my disciple' -> https://hinduismtoday.com/magazine/july-1991/1991-07-last-bhairav-master-will-teach-until-year-2006/

'Through viewing this!'; 'They will be initiated by themselves'; 1990 Gita commentary; recordings to be transcribed and published -> https://lakshmanjooacademy.org/blog/how-will-people-be-initiated-in-kashmir-shaivism
'There is no question of deserving. Grace can shine on anybody.' -> https://www.lakshmanjooacademy.org/blog/why-doesnt-lord-shiva-give-grace-to-everyone-grace-in-kashmir-shaivism%2F
annual havan at Ishwar Ashram, Srinagar; 'Great Sage of Ishber' -> https://ishwarashramtrust.com/about
Sanderson six years in Kashmir with Lakshman Joo -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Sanderson
krishnamacharya: born 18 Nov 1888 Muchukundapura; died 28 Feb 1989 Madras; eldest of six; father died when he was ten; Mysore at 12, Parakala Matha; Banaras 1906; Queen's College, Patna; Irwin, Simla, 1919; Kailash cave; married Namagiriamma 1925; coffee plantation Hasan; Maharaja in Banaras 1926; Town Hall 1931; yogashala 11 Aug 1933; Yoga Makaranda 1934; Yogasanagalu c. 1941; closed 1950; Madras 1952; Vivekananda College; Goldberg on abuse; 'Teach what is appropriate for an individual' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirumalai_Krishnamacharya
Iyengar: 'those few days determined what I have become today'; joined 1934 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._K._S._Iyengar

Iyengar: 'He would hit us hard on our backs as if with iron rods' (Astadala Yogamala 1:52) -> https://yogaanatomy.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Seizing-the-Whip-B.-K.-S.-Iyengar-and-the-Making-of-Modern-Yoga-.-Eric-Shaw.-December-2016.pdf

Desikachar 1995: 'What makes my father's yoga teachings unique is his insistence on attending to each individual and to his or her uniqueness.' -> https://www.yogajournal.com/yoga-101/philosophy/krishnamacharya/
Pagés Ruiz: five conflicting Korunta accounts; 1920s demonstrations (pulse, cars, teeth) -> https://www.yogajournal.com/yoga-101/history-of-yoga/krishnamacharya-s-legacy/
Korunta found in Calcutta University Library, later damaged by ants -> https://www.ashtangayoga.info/ashtangayoga/spot-on-tradition/111998-roots-of-a-tradition/
Singleton: not cited in Yoga Makaranda; surprising no copies -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoga_Korunta

1938 film, 57 min, sponsored by Maharaja, young Iyengar, 'may be the earliest footage of harmoniously linked postures' -> https://asia.si.edu/explore-art-culture/video/yoga-the-art-of-transformation/t-krishnamacharya-asanas
K.V. Iyer gymnasium next to yogasala; silent film for national circulation; Sritattvanidhi -> https://wellcomecollection.org/stories/yoga-adapts-to-time-and-place
Sjoman 1996/1999 Abhinav; 122 asanas; Vyayama Dipika; ropes, mallakhamba; Singleton compares to Bukh -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yoga_Tradition_of_the_Mysore_Palace

Singleton preface: no plagiarism claim, 'adaptation, reframing, reinterpretation'; hostile criticism; ashtanga dandavat; Gourley 'a bold and stunning hypothesis' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoga_Body
